Government Satcom Programmes, Tenders and RFP Portals to Track: Europe and Asia-Pacific

GovernmentDefenseEuropeLEO Satellite

A guide to official government and defence procurement portals and to ongoing and upcoming sovereign and military satcom programmes in Europe and Asia-Pacific, as of November 12, 2026. It lists 70 official RFP portals (EU/NATO, national European, Asia-Pacific and multilateral, each curl-checked), 45 programmes, and a 24-row watchlist sorted by next milestone. Near-term closings include NCIA’s Augmentation SATCOM Services (Nov 16 and 23, 2026) and Australia’s JP9102 follow-ons; the large European decisions still ahead are Germany’s SATCOMBw Stage 4 award and IRIS² sub-tier work on the ground segment and Low-LEO layer. Asia-Pacific coverage includes Japan’s awarded J-LEO and Mitsubishi Electric X-band follow-on, and Korea’s military satcom plans.

Government Satcom Programmes, Tenders and RFP Portals to Track: Europe and Asia-Pacific

Ongoing and upcoming sovereign/military satcom programmes, open and upcoming RFPs/RFIs (including ground, terminal and managed-service sub-tiers), and the official procurement portals behind them | Status as of November 12, 2026

Prepared for Paul. Citations in square brackets are clickable and map to the numbered References. Portal links in Section 1 are clickable directly. Status labels: OPEN · RFI / MARKET ENGAGEMENT · PENDING AWARD · AWARDED · PLANNED · Items marked [UNVERIFIED] come only from press, analyst or aggregator sources with no official confirmation found. Deadlines are as published by the buyer, in the buyer’s local time zone.

Executive summary

  • The near-term bid calendar is concentrated in NATO, the EDA and Australia. Closing in the next ten weeks: NCIA’s Augmentation SATCOM Services framework (IFB-CO-424244-SATCOM, bids close Nov 16 for Work Packages 1–2 and Nov 23, 2026 for Work Package 3) [16,17]; NCIA’s Next Generation SATCOM Capability Programme Package RFI (RFI-42634128-SATCOM, responses due Dec 3, 2026, with an industry workshop at NATO Edge, Izmir, Nov 17–19) [19]; Australia’s SPA9102 LOE2 narrowband UHF GEO RFT (ADSS/RFT/84124/1, closes Dec 7, 2026) [72]; the UK MOD’s UAV SATCOM market engagement (engagement deadline Dec 11, 2026) [23]; and the EDA’s €450M satcom framework contract (EDA/2026/OP/0011, deadline Jan 22, 2027) [13,14].
  • The two big European sovereign constellation decisions are both late-2026/early-2027 events. Germany’s SATCOMBw Stage 4 (about €10bn, about 200 satellites, about 40 in service from 2029) was expected to be awarded around the end of 2026 [25]; one analyst (Nov 10, 2026) now sees a ministry decision possibly this year, with early 2027 still plausible [26]. The UK’s £2.4bn SKYNET 6 Wideband Satellite System award (Airbus vs Lockheed Martin) is under Prime Ministerial review; the MOD says “no final decisions have been made” [22].
  • IRIS² is now a supply-chain opportunity, not a prime-contract one. All 348 satellites are ordered [1,3,4]. Remaining entry points are: the ground segment under Hispasat as prime (more than €1.6bn) [5,6]; the Low-LEO layer, whose procurement plan is on esa-star [7], with ESA’s Low-LEO ITT#2 planned for Q1 2027 and contracts targeted for Q3 2027 [8]; and Ka-band user terminals, where a €20M Commission grant call closed on Aug 26, 2026 with grant signature planned for Nov–Dec 2026 [9,10].
  • Asia-Pacific is dominated by awarded national programmes with sub-tier follow-on. Japan’s J-LEO went to Rakuten (RAST) and is moving into build-out through the new Rakuten AST JV [53,55]. Japan’s MoD contracted Mitsubishi Electric for the next X-band defence satellite at ¥123.53bn [56]. South Korea approved the Military Satcom System-III GEO programme at about KRW 1.27 trillion for 2026–2032 [61], and is studying a sovereign LEO network by 2035 sized at 128–512 satellites (about KRW 4–14 trillion) [64]. India’s Army satellite GSAT-7B is expected around mid-2028 [69]. Taiwan’s first B5G LEO satellite has slipped to a 2028 launch [79], and TASA has live component tenders this month [80].
  • Upcoming (not yet tendered) to watch for 2027–2028: a Greek MILSATCOM GEO system (about €400M, SAFE-financed, tender not yet announced as of April 2026) [43]; France’s Syracuse V (studies urged from 2027 in a multi-orbit LEO–GEO approach) [24]; Italy’s Mercurio LEO constellation (Phase 2 industrial contracts, full operation not before 2031) [33]; Poland’s MILSATCOM (ICEYE–PGZ concept, 2026–2030) [41]; Korea’s LEO budget line (being considered as a new 2027 project) [64]; and Indonesia’s SATRIA-2 (still at demand analysis, financing undecided) [82].
  • Portals: Section 1 lists 70 official portals. In practice TED (with CPV 32530000/32531000 filters), esa-star, NCIA NEO, the EDA page and AusTender carried most of the open satcom opportunities found this month. Several portals block automated access (NCIA, NSPA, EDA, INAPROC, ePerolehan, ADB return 403; TED returns a 202 bot check). They open normally in a browser, and each is flagged in the table.

2. Europe: ongoing and upcoming government satcom programmes and tenders

2.1 EU, ESA and NATO

Programme

Status as of Nov 2026 (sourced)

Opportunity / sub-tier

IRIS² – constellation and satellites (EU/ESA/SpaceRISE)

AWARDED. Concession signed Dec 2024; Aug 2026 ‘Rendezvous 1’ added 66 military satellites (348 total); services start progressively from 2029 [1,2]. Satellite manufacturing contracts placed Aug–Sep 2026 [3,4].

Prime work is closed. Sub-tier supply to the satellite primes (Airbus, Thales Alenia Space, OHB, Aerospacelab) continues.

IRIS² – ground segment (Hispasat as prime)

AWARDED (prime) / sub-tier ongoing. Hispasat named prime for antennas, control systems and ground-network connections, budget above €1.6bn (Aug 7, 2026) [5]. SpaceRISE procures the ground segment in four lots: EU gateways, a cloud-native mission control centre, a service lot, and a control lot with the S3C, overseas TT&C and data backbone [6].

Gateway sites, TT&C antennas, mission-control software and security equipment through Hispasat and the lot winners.

IRIS² – Low-LEO layer (led by Hispasat)

OPEN (procurement plan) → ITT Q1 2027. Procurement plan published on esa-star; RFP launched after the April 2026 Info Days [7]. ESA Low-LEO Implementation Phase ITT#2 (Phases B2/C/D/E/F) is planned for Q1 2027, with M1/M2.1/M2.2 contracts targeted for Q3 2027. Taking part in ITT#1 is not a prerequisite [8].

Space, ground and user-segment demonstrators. Best near-term entry point for SMEs.

IRIS²/GOVSATCOM user terminals (PPPA-2026-IRIS2-UT-INDREADY)

CLOSED – evaluation. €20M, up to 3 projects, Ka-band (commercial and military) terminal industrialisation. Deadline Aug 26, 2026; grant agreements planned Nov–Dec 2026 [9,10].

Watch the Funding & Tenders Portal for follow-on terminal calls.

EU GOVSATCOM

OPERATING / pooling. Pools Member State governmental satcom capacity for authorised users. The Commission said it would present a European Space Shield plan later in 2026, with delivery targeted as early as 2027 [11].

EUSPA hub-support tenders. National capacity providers can offer capacity into the pool.

EDA Satcom Framework Contract (EDA/2026/OP/0011, 26.ISE.JP.001)

OPEN. Single framework, estimated €450M: raw capacity, anchoring, backhaul, managed services, earth stations and terminals, commercial crypto. Published Oct 22, 2026; deadline Jan 22, 2027 [13,14].

Managed-service and capacity resellers, teleport operators, terminal OEMs.

ESA Connectivity & Secure Communications (ARTES 4.0, Moonlight, IRIS² element)

FUNDED. €2.1bn subscribed at CM25 [12].

Rolling ESA ITTs and ARTES calls on esa-star.

NCIA Augmentation SATCOM Services (IFB-CO-424244-SATCOM)

OPEN – closing. Pre-competed IDIQ for commercial satcom on an ‘as needed’ basis. Estimated €8,071,406 per year for 5 years plus €15,497,882 for commissioning and hardware; 70/30 technical/price best value [17]. Bids close Nov 16, 2026 (WP1, WP2) and Nov 23, 2026 (WP3); planned award Dec 29, 2026 [16,15].

Capacity, satcom telephony and turnkey deployable HQ solutions. Needs national eligibility.

NCIA Next Generation SATCOM CPP (RFI-42634128-SATCOM)

RFI. Market research for next-generation satcom services and systems across GEO, MEO, LEO and HEO, multi-orbit terminals, NATO-controlled key management, and resilience. Responses due Dec 3, 2026, 12:00 CET; workshop at NATO Edge, Izmir, Nov 17–19, 2026; NATO-country respondents only [19,18].

Shapes NATO’s next big satcom acquisition. High priority to respond.

NSPA GCC SATCOM Support Partnership

AWARDED (vehicle). First award: SES O3b mPOWER MEO Global Services, 3-year IDIQ worth USD 200M plus two 1-year options (Sep 2024), under the US–Luxembourg partnership set up in 2022 [20].

Further capacity orders under the partnership; check NSPA for new lots.

NATO HALO (Hybrid Alliance Layered Operations in Space)

PLANNED. Canada, Denmark, Finland, Germany, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and Türkiye announced (Jul 7, 2026) a federated ‘mega constellation’ of nationally owned military satellites [21].

No procurement found yet. Watch national MoD portals of the 8 nations.

2.2 National European programmes

Programme

Status as of Nov 2026 (sourced)

Opportunity / sub-tier

UK – SKYNET 6 Enduring Capability: Wideband Satellite System (WSS)

PENDING AWARD. £2.4bn; Airbus Defence and Space UK vs Lockheed Martin UK; two tranches of GEO satellites with X-band and Mil-Ka payloads plus new ground and launch. MOD (Nov 10, 2026): “no final decisions have been made”. The sister Narrowband Satellite System (NSS) was cancelled in favour of extending SKYNET 5 and ‘space as a service’ [22].

Post-award UK supply chain (Stevenage/Portsmouth if Airbus; Durham hub if LM) [22]. Narrowband ‘as-a-service’ routes are a future opening.

UK – MOD SATCOM for UAV platforms (2026/S 000-098697)

RFI / MARKET ENGAGEMENT. Low-SWaP beyond-line-of-sight satcom for UAVs; CPV 32531000; engagement deadline Dec 11, 2026; indicative contract 1 Apr 2027 [23].

Terminal OEMs and LEO/GEO service providers.

France – Syracuse V

PLANNED. A 2026 amendment to the LPM update bill says Syracuse V was planned in LPM 2024–2030 and urges development studies from 2027 in a multi-orbit LEO–GEO approach. It notes the end of Sicral 2 by 2030 and of the first Syracuse IV in 2036 [24]. (This is an amendment text, not confirmation of a contract.)

Watch DGA notices on PLACE/BOAMP for study contracts.

Germany – SATCOMBw Stage 4 (LEO, sovereign)

PENDING AWARD. About €10bn, about 200 satellites, about 40 initially from 2029; award expected around end-2026 [25]. OHB–Rheinmetall JV formed Jun 2026 [27]. Berenberg (Nov 10, 2026) sees a ministry decision possibly this year [26]. Tender is classified (see the earlier IRIS²/SATCOMBw report).

Sub-tier through the OHB–Rheinmetall JV (and Airbus, per government and industry sources) [25].

Germany – Bundeswehr satellite ground segment (deployable)

RFI / MARKET ENGAGEMENT. German Space Agency at DLR market survey (not a tender) for a turnkey, deployable ground segment to control Bundeswehr satellites from LEO to GEO (TED 657032-2026, Sep 23, 2026) [29]. Parallel survey on ground-based counter-space systems (658475-2026) [30].

Ground-segment integrators and TT&C suppliers. Watch for the follow-on formal procedure on service.bund.de/e-Vergabe.

Germany – SATCOMBw Stage 3

AWARDED. Airbus, about €2.1bn (2024) for two GEO military satellites and ground [28].

Ground/terminal sustainment.

Italy – SICRAL 3

AWARDED (in build). DPP 2025–2027 allocates €288.29M to 2029 on top of €320M (ordinary budget and MIMIT) and €211M from the 2025 Budget Law [31]. Two satellites to launch on Falcon 9 in 2027 [32].

Ground segment (Telespazio) and terminals.

Italy – ‘Mercurio’ / defence LEO constellation

PLANNED. Dual-use LEO constellation. The feasibility study finished in 2025 and the project is in ‘Phase 2’ to define industrial contracts; full operation not before 2031 [33]. The DPP funds LEO study and design [31].

Leonardo/Telespazio/Thales Alenia Space-led. Watch ASI and Segredifesa.

Italy – LEO broadband services (Guardia di Finanza) / Air Force OneWeb

RFI – GdF market consultation for LEO broadband services published May 27, 2026 [34]. CLOSED – Air Force OneWeb connectivity and subscription, €161,290, deadline Sep 18, 2026 (TED 606826-2026) [35].

Managed LEO services for security forces.

Spain – SpainSat NG-III (replacement for NG-II)

AWARDED. Airbus prime (X-band); Thales Alenia Space Spain (UHF, Mil-Ka); launch Q3 2030, operational early 2031 [36]. Council of Ministers (Oct 27, 2026) approved a €492.2M loan profile to Hisdesat for 2026–2030; PAZ 2 is funded from the same line [37].

Spanish ground and terminal sub-tier.

Luxembourg – GovSat-2

AWARDED. Thales Alenia Space GEO satellite, X/Ka/UHF (Jul 24, 2025) [38]. Luxembourg Defence direct award to LuxGovSat of €215M for satcom capacity (contract Feb 26, 2026) [39].

Capacity resale to NATO/EU partners.

Poland – terminals and MILSATCOM

AWARDED – Armament Agency–GISS: 157 Medium Satellite Terminals, PLN 2.4bn, signed May 29, 2026 under SAFE [40]. PLANNED – ICEYE–PGZ letter of intent (Sep 11, 2026) for a sovereign, distributed MILSATCOM; programme planned for 2026–2030 with full operational capability at the end of that period [41]. Unit 2305 satellite terminals plus data service tender (TED 582663-2026) [42].

A future MILSATCOM competition; watch Agencja Uzbrojenia and e-Zamówienia.

Greece – national MILSATCOM

PLANNED. About €400M integrated MILSATCOM incl. a GEO satellite; tender not yet announced (Apr 2026); SAFE funding and a 2024 RFI; Airbus–GEK Terna teaming [43]. Space Operations Command inaugurated and national MILSATCOM plan announced (Nov 10, 2026) [44].

Prime bid expected; watch the Hellenic MoD and TED.

Norway – FMA commercial satcom framework

AWARDED/IN PROCUREMENT. Framework up to NOK 450M, Jul 6, 2026 – Jul 5, 2033: Iridium, Viasat, Thuraya, OneWeb, Starlink, later Starshield, Amazon Leo, Lightspeed; prequalification closed Apr 20, 2026 [45].

Distributor/reseller framework.

CLOSED – MoD LEO satcom kits framework, 2 lots, RON 5.29M est. (deadline Sep 28, 2026) [46]. AWARDED – MAI satcom infrastructure, terminals and services, 48-month framework, listed value RON 179.36M [47].

Terminal and service resellers.

OPEN. Satellite communication equipment and access administration; deadline Dec 3, 2026 (TED 742977-2026) [48].

Small managed-service opportunity.

RFI / MARKET ENGAGEMENT. Open market consultation on the space domain with follow-up dialogue sessions (TED 744960-2026, Oct 27, 2026) [49].

Positioning for Dutch HALO and Arctic-satcom contributions [21].

Czechia – Ministry of the Interior satcom

CLOSED. 410 satellite phones, 410 satellite-internet antennas and 410 rugged cases; deadline Oct 19, 2026 (TED 637715-2026) [50].

Indicator of continuing civil-protection demand.

Ground and terminal follow-ons via ATLA.

South Korea – Military Satcom System-III (ANASIS-II follow-on)

PLANNED (basic plan approved). DAPA approved the basic plan on May 22, 2026: GEO military satellite plus control/terminal ground segment, ADD-led R&D, 2026–2032, about KRW 1.27 trillion [61,62].

Industry partners under ADD; watch D2B/DAPA. No prime named in sources found.

South Korea – sovereign LEO satcom network

PLANNED. Inter-agency task force since March 2026 (MSIT, KASA, MND, DAPA) [63]. Target: build by 2035. Scenarios: 128 satellites (about KRW 4T), 256 (about KRW 7.4T), 512 (about KRW 14T); a related budget is being considered as a new 2027 project [64]. The Deputy PM urged faster development (Oct 2026) [66].

Early positioning (Hanwha/MDA/Telesat teaming in the earlier Korea report).

South Korea – 6G LEO satcom technology programme (MSIT/KASA)

UNDER WAY (R&D). KRW 320bn over 6 years (KRW 300.4bn state); 2 LEO satellites plus ground and terminal stations; call ran Feb 28 – Mar 31, 2025 via IITP [65].

Component and terminal suppliers to the selected teams.

India – GSAT-7B (Army)

AWARDED. MoD–NSIL contract (about ₹3,000 crore, Mar 29, 2023) [68]; launch expected around mid-2028 [69].

Ground terminals via defproc/GeM.

India – GSAT-7R (Navy)

LAUNCHED Nov 2, 2025; about 4,400 kg, Indian Ocean Region coverage [67].

Shipborne terminal buys.

India – ISRO/IN-SPACe EoIs

CLOSED. SAC EOI for optical communication terminals for LEO and GEO satellites, due Jun 10, 2026 [70]. IN-SPACe EoI for up to three Indian firms to run ground stations at NRSC Shadnagar (Jun 2026) [71].

Optical-comm and ground-station players.

Australia – SPA9102 (ex-JP9102)

OPEN. LOE2 narrowband UHF GEO RFT (ADSS/RFT/84124/1), published Sep 7, 2026, closes Dec 7, 2026 12:00 ACT, 5-year delivery [72]. Revives the JP9102 requirement cancelled in Nov 2024, about 15 months after an RFI [74]. Four lines of effort: wideband, narrowband, ground control, alternatives; 2026 IIP: A$5.2–7.2bn over a decade; about 10-year satellite life sought [73].

LOE1 wideband and LOE3 ground control are the next RFTs to watch [73].

Australia – NBN Sky Muster replacement (Amazon Leo)

AWARDED / delayed. NBN LEO service milestone (Aug 27, 2026) [75]; launch of plans pushed to after mid-2027 [76].

Installer and terminal-logistics sub-tier.

Singapore – DSTA direct-to-device (D2D) demonstration

AWARDED. DSTA contract with AST SpaceMobile (Mar 23, 2026) to demonstrate space-based cellular broadband for HADR and emergencies [77].

Watch GeBIZ for follow-ons.

Taiwan – TASA B5G LEO communications satellites (1A/1B)

AWARDED + OPEN components. The 1A Ka-band payload went to CesiumAstro (budget NT$880M) [78]; first launch now planned for 2028 (was 2027) [79]. Live TASA tenders include TASA-P-1150815 B5G satellite battery engineering model (opening Nov 17, 2026) [80].

Component and ground-station tenders on TASA and PCC.

Indonesia – SATRIA-2 (BAKTI Komdigi)

PLANNED. National Strategic Project; BAKTI prioritising demand analysis before choosing a financing scheme (latest found: Dec 10, 2025) [81,82].

Possible PPP (KPBU); watch BAKTI and INAPROC.

Philippines – DICT LEO connectivity for GIDAs

CLOSED. ₱179.49M contract for LEO internet at 396 Luzon and 191 Visayas/Mindanao sites; bids due Jul 27, 2026 [83].

LEO resellers; watch PhilGEPS for rebids.

Gaps. No 2026 government satcom tender was found for Vietnam, Malaysia or Thailand in this search. Vietnam has a VINASAT-3 plan, but no tender was found. None of these sources were fetched, so none are cited. QZSS and Korea’s KPS are navigation, not satcom, and are excluded.

How to use this watchlist

  • Set three automated searches now: (1) TED, CPV 32530000 and 32531000, filtered to defence buyers; (2) NCIA NEO plus SAM.gov for “SATCOM”; (3) AusTender, category 25150000 (Spacecraft). Together these surfaced most of the live items in this report.
  • Register early where eligibility is gated: NCIA needs a national Declaration of Eligibility via the NATO delegation [17]; esa-star needs an entity record before any IRIS² ITT; Korea D2B/KONEPS and India defproc/CPPP need local digital certificates; Japan needs the 全省庁統一資格 unified qualification.
  • Sub-tier routes matter more than prime bids in 2027: IRIS² ground segment (Hispasat) [5], Low-LEO (ESA ITT#2) [8], SATCOMBw Stage 4 through the OHB–Rheinmetall JV [27], and J-LEO through Rakuten AST [55].

Caveats

  • NCIA pages sit behind a Cloudflare check. Bid-closing dates for IFB-CO-424244 (Nov 16/23, 2026; planned award Dec 29, 2026) come from a verbatim mirror of the NCIA page dated Oct 27, 2026 [16]. Confirm them on NEO before bidding, because NCIA often amends dates (the mirror references Amendment 7).
  • The NOI’s value estimate for IFB-CO-424244 covers only one potential user group as of 2028 [17], so total call-off value could be higher.
  • SATCOMBw Stage 4, SKYNET 6 WSS award timing, Greek MILSATCOM size, Italian Mercurio timing and Polish MILSATCOM come from press or company statements, not official tender documents. Treat them as indicative.
  • The Norway framework is cited via an aggregator of the Doffin notice [45]. Search Doffin for “satellittkommunikasjonstjenester” to get the official notice.
  • Indonesia SATRIA-2: no update newer than Dec 2025 was found.
  • This report focuses on government and defence buyers. Commercial-operator procurements (e.g., Eutelsat’s or SES’s own buys) are covered only where they are part of a government concession.
